market_view: Calm bull regime persists as of 2026-06-11. AI capex super-cycle drives semiconductor and infrastructure spending. Rate path stabilizing supports REITs and infrastructure. International equity (Taiwan/Asia) outperforms on AI supply-chain tailwinds. Credit spreads tight (HYG not distressed), reinforcing risk-on tilt. Dominant 21-day risk: sudden shock to AI capex expectations or Treasury yield spike above 4.67%.
regime_assessment: Calm bull confirmed by VNQ 52-week high, tight HY spreads, EWT/TSMC AI-capex momentum. Historically rewards momentum continuation in quality growth, selective international equity with earnings momentum, infrastructure/REIT as rates stabilize, and managed futures as low-correlation ballast. Unusual concentration in AI/Taiwan supply chain creates idiosyncratic risk vs. typical calm-bull episodes.
quant_baseline_summary: Quant signals broadly support risk-on positioning with momentum continuation in EWT, MGM, MU, JEF, STLD, HAE, ORA, and SJM. Defensive ballast (BIL, HYG, KMLM) provides portfolio-level Sharpe improvement. DBB and MPC add commodity/energy diversification consistent with broadening bull thesis.

key_risks: TSMC AI capex guidance cut on next earnings would crater EWT and MU simultaneously — ~20% of portfolio exposed
US 10-year Treasury yield breaking above 4.67% compresses multiples on rate-sensitive positions (VNQ, IFRA, ORA) — ~23% of portfolio
MGM privatization bid withdrawal would cause 10-15% drawdown in that position
China macro weakness (PMI <49) would hit DBB and indirectly EWT through Asia supply chain
MU earnings miss on June 24 is a near-term binary risk — sized at 8% to contain damage
what_could_be_wrong: The biggest risk is that I'm overweight a narrow AI capex theme (EWT + MU = 20%) in a regime that rewards breadth. If TSMC or Micron disappoint on AI-specific revenue, the concentrated exposure could cause outsized drawdown. Additionally, the MGM privatization bid may not materialize into a firm offer, creating deal-break downside. The calm bull regime could transition to stressed if a geopolitical shock (Taiwan Strait, tariff escalation) materializes suddenly.
